title: Control no more than one TV, or two radio, licences in an area
what: A person must not be in a position to control more than one commercial television licence, or more than two commercial radio licences, in the same licence area.

sources.title: Broadcasting Services Act 1992 (Cth)
sources.quote: 53 Limitation on control of commercial television broadcasting licences A person must not be in a position to exercise control of more than one commercial television broadcasting licence in the same licence area.

sources.title: Broadcasting Services Act 1992 (Cth)
sources.quote: 54 Limitation on control of commercial radio broadcasting licences A person must not be in a position to exercise control of more than 2 commercial radio broadcasting licences in the same licence area.

reach.condition: only owners of commercial broadcasting licences

sources.title: Broadcasting Services Act 1992 (Cth)
sources.quote: 53 Limitation on control of commercial television broadcasting licences A person must not be in a position to exercise control of more than one commercial television broadcasting licence in the same licence area.

assessment.summary: No one may control more than one commercial television licence, or more than two commercial radio licences, in the same licence area. The limits aim at diversity of voices; they also block mergers that might lower costs, and the number of licences in each area is itself limited.

marks.reason: Stops one owner taking every commercial licence in an area.
Blocks consolidation within a licence area, which could lower costs for regional broadcasters.

assessment.confidence_note: Whether the limits raise or lower productivity is contested; the marks offset.
